Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
A Matrimonial Suit (Case No.110 of 
2021) was filed by the appellant-plaintiff 
under Section 13(1)(i-a)(i-b) of the 
Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The suit was 
dismissed. A Civil Appeal (Civil Appeal 
No.07 of 2023) was filed. The said 
Appeal has been dismissed vide 
judgment dated 22.12.2023, passed by 
learned District Judge, Pithoragarh. 
2. Heard Mr. Harshit Sanwal, learned 
counsel for appellant. 
3. In the facts and circumstances of 
the case, it seems appropriate to direct
the parties to appear before this Court 
in-person before passing any order on 
Admission. 
4. Issue notice to respondent. 
5. Steps to be taken within three days.  6. List on 10.04.2024. 
7. Both, appellant-Rajendra Singh Airi 
and respondent-Nanda Devi are directed
to appear in-person before this Court 
either through video conferencing or 
physically.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.)

D/42 SA No.20 of 2024
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
 Mr. R.S. Sammal, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. Harshit Sanwal, 
Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. Akshay Joshi, Advocate for the 
respondent.
 The appellant filed a suit for divorce 
against the respondent, which was 
registered as Matrimonial Suit No.110 
of 2021, Rajendra Singh Airi Vs. Smt. 
Nanda Devi, in the court of Civil Judge 
(Sr. Div.), Pithoragarh (“the case”). But, 
the case was dismissed on 30.09.2023, 
which was challenged by the appellant 
in Civil Appeal No.7 of 2023, Rajendra 
Singh Airi Vs. Smt. Nanda Devi, in the 
court of District Judge, Pithoragarh 
(“the appeal”). The appeal was 
dismissed on 22.12.2023.
 Heard on admission.
 Learned counsel for the appellant 
would submit that the appellant and 
respondent, both are staying separate 
since 2017. There is continuous 
separation and the marriage has 
become fiction. 
 Learned counsel for the appellant 
would submit that in view of the law as 
laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court in the case of Rakesh Raman Vs. 
Kavita, AIR 2023 SC 2144, this mass 
separation amounts to cruelty. It is 
submitted that under the admitted 
facts, this law has not been considered  and this is the substantial question of 
law in this second appeal. 
 The appeal is admitted on the 
following substantial questions of law:-
(i) Whether the courts below 
committed an error and failed 
to exercise jurisdiction as long 
period of separation coupled 
with the absence of 
cohabitation amounts to 
cruelty, which is a valid 
ground for divorce under 
Section 13 of the Hindu 
Marriage Act, 1955.
 Call for the lower court record.
 List for final hearing on 16.07.2026. 
 
(Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 04.06.2026
Sanjay

50D UKHC010019752024
SA No. 20 of 2024
Rajendra Singh Airi .…… Appellant
Vs.
Nanda Devi ……Respondents
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Harshit Sanwal, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mr. Akshay Joshi, Advocate for the 
respondent.
This is second appeal arising out of 
matrimonial discord. The husband seeks 
divorce, which has not been held.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits 
that the parties are staying separate for more 
than nine years now. It is a case of irretrievable 
break down of marriage and there has been no 
cohabitation for approximately nine years. 
Hence, it amounts to cruelty.
Before any decision is taken, this Court is 
of the view that one more effort should be made 
for settlement that may arrive between the 
parties.
List on 21.08.2026 at 10:30 a.m.
On that date, parties shall appear in 
person before this Court.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 07.08.2026
Jitendra
